question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund is an OPEN-ENDED Category III AIF. What is the appropriate NAV publication frequency that the fund administrator should adopt?

answer.text: Monthly NAV by the 10th of next month
Quarterly NAV in line with Cat I/II practice
Daily NAV reflecting mark-to-market of listed and exchange-traded derivatives
Annual NAV audited by the statutory auditor

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Open-ended Cat III AIFs must declare NAV daily to support redemption/subscription cycles. NAV excludes borrowed funds and is marked-to-market using closing prices for listed securities and exchange-traded derivatives. Fund administrator publishes NAV on T+1 typically. **The Trap:** Options A and B are Cat I/II (illiquid PE/VC) frequencies. Option D is the audit cadence, not NAV publication. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D tests Cat I/II quarterly/semi-annual valuation. XIX-E fixes on daily NAV for Cat III open-ended. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Cut-off for subscriptions/redemptions is typically T, with NAV computed on T and transactions priced at T NAV (dealing day). Coordinate with prime broker margin cycle and equalisation credit/debit for new investors subscribing mid-accounting-period.
